title: &aLast Light
subtitle: A shrine makes a place you come back to. The rest makes it home.

quests.title: &aA Home Worth Defending
quests.subtitle: Last Light needs more than a fire.
description: &o"A shrine makes a place you come back to. A table makes it a place you'd want to."&r
Craft a &6table&r and a &6chair&r from any wood. Handcrafted furniture can be sat on, set with plates and cups, and dressed with cushions and sheets.
The village has a name now. Give it a hall.

quests.title: A Bed Worth Waking In
quests.subtitle: You can't die for good. You can at least sleep well.
description: A &6fancy bed&r takes planks, wool, a &6cushion&r and a &6sheet&r. It does what a bed does, with more dignity.
Sleeping in a bed sets your respawn, so keep it within sight of the shrine.

quests.title: Trophy Wall
quests.subtitle: Proof, mounted.
description: Handcrafted &6trophies&r are made from what you take off the dead: a spider's eye, a skeleton's skull, a creeper's head, a phantom's membrane.
Hang one above the shrine. The Keeper won't say anything. The Keeper will look at it.

quests.title: Flax and String
quests.subtitle: Supplies need somewhere to live.
description: &6Flax&r grows wild here and there and plants like any crop. Weave it with string into a &6Sack&r: a bag you can set down, pick up and carry with everything still inside.
Sacks are heavy. So is dying with everything you own in your pockets.

quests.title: Glass and Patience
quests.subtitle: Keep what's precious where you can see it.
description: A &6Jar&r stores what bowls, bottles and buckets carry (honey, soup, potions, water), a stack of cookies, or a small living thing.
Some Ashborn keep a jar of honey by the shrine. Some keep a jar of something that glows.

quests.title: A Quiver Taken Back
quests.subtitle: The skeletons won't need it.
description: Some skeletons rise with a &6Quiver&r on their backs. Kill them and it's yours. Dungeon chests and pillager camps hide a few more.
A quiver holds several kinds of arrow and lets you choose which one to loose. Carry it in your offhand or an accessory slot.

quests.title: The World as It Was
quests.subtitle: Round, and lit. Imagine that.
description: The &6Wandering Trader&r still carries &6Globes&r, painted back when the world had a sun to turn under. Buy one and set it somewhere in Last Light.
Spin it. Nobody's stopping you.

quests.title: Walls in an Afternoon
quests.subtitle: The dark can count. Make it count bricks.
description: An &6Iron Wand&r (Ashen Alloy, redstone and a stick) extends the face you click: one course of wall becomes two, two become ten. It draws blocks from your inventory, shulker boxes and bundles.
It can undo its last placements, too (see &eControls&r). Everyone builds a wall in the wrong place once.

quests.title: The Architect's Core
quests.subtitle: Lines, walls, rings. Geometry against the dark.
description: Craft an &6Architect Core&r (glass panes, amethyst and a compass) and combine it with your wand in a crafting grid. Click two corners for a line, wall, floor, box or cube; click a centre, then an edge, for a circle or a ring.
&7Angel, Exchange and Destruction cores fit the same way.
A ring of stone around Last Light won't stop a Sovereign. It will stop most of what comes before one.

quests.title: Everyone's Share
quests.subtitle: The dead hoard. Fairly, now.
description: Loot chests in dungeons, ruins and towers are &6per-player&r: everyone who opens one gets their own roll, and nobody takes a companion's share.
Open ten of them. A loot chest looks different once you've opened it, so you always know which ones are left.

quests.title: Rest on the Road
quests.subtitle: Skip the night. Keep your shrine.
description: A &6Sleeping Bag&r lets you sleep through the night wherever you unroll it, and it doesn't move your respawn. Your shrine stays your shrine.
&7You can't sleep with monsters nearby. On a Hunter's Moon, there are always monsters nearby.

quests.title: The Night Shift
quests.subtitle: Some hunts only happen after dark.
description: Hang a &6Hammock&r between two &6Rope and Nails&r and you can sleep through the &oday&r instead.
For Ashborn who prefer to hunt when the hunting is good.

quests.title: A Favour for a Friend
quests.subtitle: The villagers have problems too. Smaller ones.
description: The villagers of Last Light talk. Stand close and say something in chat; they answer in speech bubbles. Ask one for work.
Accept the request (&e/villagerai request accept&r) and see it through: fetch what they need, or kill what's bothering them. They pay in emeralds, and they remember.

quests.title: Hero of the Village Square
quests.subtitle: Ten favours. They'll name a well after you.
description: Finish &6ten&r villager requests. Word spreads: your standing climbs from stranger to friend to &6hero&r, and heroes get better prices.
&7Gossip carries about 48 blocks. So does a bad reputation.

quests.title: Last Light Takes Up Arms
quests.subtitle: Villages that fight back live longer.
description: Give a sword to a villager with no profession and they become a &6Guard&r: armoured, patrolling, loyal to the bell.
Guards are not sellswords. They won't follow you out. That's rather the point.
